entries.title: Mike Lindell Vows to Appeal Minnesota Loss to the U.S. Supreme Court
entries.summary: The MyPillow founder said he would appeal his primary loss after Minnesota’s top court rejected his case.
entries.content:
MyPillow founder Mike Lindell said he would appeal his loss in Minnesota’s Republican gubernatorial primary to the U.S. Supreme Court after the state’s top court rejected his recount bid.

“My name was on 1,100,000 ballots and they all need to be looked at and counted,” he told the St. Paul TV station KTSP on Saturday. He told NBC News that he would appeal the Minnesota Supreme Court ruling no matter the cost.

That court earlier Saturday denied Lindell’s petition for a recount in the primary for governor, which he lost to Minnesota House Speaker Lisa Demuth by some 45,000 votes.

Lindell, who had been endorsed by President Donald Trump, had said he would independently pay the full costs of a recount, estimated at $825,000, but he did not pay by the state’s deadline. He said he was refusing after learning the audit would have examined only those ballots cast for him or Demuth, and not the other primary candidates.

In the six-page decision issued Saturday night, Minnesota Chief Justice Natalie Hudson wrote that Lindell’s claim “fails on the merits.”

Hudson said the Minnesota secretary of state’s office had provided a recount plan that is lawful and that does not commit “any wrongful act, omission, or error,” refuting Lindell’s claim.

Lindell filed a lawsuit last week against the Minnesota State Canvassing Board and Steve Simon, the state’s top election official. Lindell has spread widely debunked claims of election fraud, including that Trump won the 2020 election, and previously faced a $1.3 billion defamation lawsuit from Dominion Voting Systems.

In his own bid for elected office this year, he began questioning incoming predictions on election night, saying about The Associated Press race calls, “What is the AP to voters? Why would I listen to the AP?”

Demuth will face Democratic Sen. Amy Klobuchar in November for the governor’s office.
entries.author: Manuela Silva

entries.title: Trump Pushes FCC to Punish Journalists Over ‘Fake Polls” and His Endorsements
entries.summary: The president said NBC’s Kristen Welker “will be reported to the FCC for rebuke or punishment” after she reported on his endorsement record.
entries.content:
President Donald Trump said NBC’s Kristen Welker “will be reported” to the Federal Communications Commission for “rebuke or punishment” after she reported that the president has had mixed results with his endorsements in races this cycle.

Welker, the host of NBC’s “Meet the Press,” said in a pretaped segment before her Sunday show that the candidates the president has backed have had varying levels of success.

“How can anyone be allowed to say this, working for freely given Public Airwaves?” Trump said on Truth Social, arguing that he has a “99% Success Rate” with endorsements. “Because of this purposeful inaccuracy, she will be reported to the FCC for rebuke or punishment. Unfortunately, she is not the only one. The Radical Left News is going out of their way to harass, demean, and libel anything ‘TRUMP.’”

Trump added that he would like FCC Chair Brendan Carr and other commissioners to take the “Threat to our Country very seriously.”

The FCC controls licenses for public airwaves, but has no authority over individual journalists or non-broadcast news outlets.

In a subsequent post, Trump lashed out at “fake polls” and said the FCC should investigate. “THE FAKE POLLS USED BY OUR CROOKED MEDIA ARE OUT OF CONTROL, AND SOMETHING MUST BE DONE ABOUT IT. FCC TO THE RESCUE!” he wrote.

Welker and Trump have sparred before, with the president walking out of an interview with the host after a tense exchange over Trump's claims that the 2020 election was rigged. It is also not the first time Trump has threatened the media — last summer, he suggested major broadcast networks should be fined or taken off the air for what he deemed to be unfavorable coverage of Republicans.

Carr has followed Trump’s directive to go after media organizations as well, ordering ABC's parent company Disney to file for early renewal of its licenses; the company sued this month, accusing the FCC of political retaliation. Carr also issued a warning to broadcasters over their coverage of the Iran war for news coverage he deemed to be “fake.”

In the past year, the president and his team have attacked numerous female journalists, including CNN’s Kaitlan Collins and Kristen Holmes, Fox News’ Shannon Bream and The New York Times’ Maggie Haberman. Back in November, when Bloomberg’s Catherine Lucey asked the president about the Epstein files, he told her to be “quiet, piggy.”

entries.title: El-Sayed Apologizes For Past Remarks About Michigan Synagogue Attack
entries.summary: The Michigan Democrat addressed a Jewish Democratic meeting after criticism for his March comments.
entries.content:
Michigan Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed apologized to Jewish Democrats for his past comments linking a terrorist attack on a Jewish synagogue earlier this year to a greater cycle of violence.

“My comments might have been misconstrued to be justifying something I did not intend to justify,” El-Sayed told reporters after speaking to the Michigan Democratic Jewish Caucus at the state Democratic Party’s nominating convention on Saturday.

“To anybody who feels like my comments might have been hurtful, I'm really sorry,” El-Sayed continued. “That was not my intention. We condemned that terrorist attack — we condemned it outright. What I was trying to do is offer context for why it happened, but it wasn’t the time for context, and you don’t ever want to trample somebody’s pain.”

According to The New York Times, El-Sayed told caucus members during the convention that he had “made a mistake.”

“I should have issued a statement, of course condemning it, and it just should have been the full stop,” the Times reported him saying.

In March, a man crashed his car into a synagogue in a suburb of Detroit and began shooting, injuring a security guard. The attacker, who was killed in the shootout, was identified as Ayman Mohamad Ghazali, a naturalized U.S. citizen from Lebanon who had lost four relatives in an Israeli airstrike in his native country a week before.

In a video condemning the attack shortly after, El-Sayed said that “hurt people hurt people” and that “violence is a cycle.”

El-Sayed’s apology comes as he is trying to unify Michigan Democrats in a tight general election race against Republican nominee Mike Rogers that may determine control of the Senate. El-Sayed continues to face backlash for campaigning with left-wing streamer Hasan Piker after a slew of lawmakers criticized Piker for comments he made about Jewish Americans.

El-Sayed won a hard-fought Democratic primary against Rep. Haley Stevens, who drew record spending from the American Israel Public Affairs Committee. El-Sayed’s criticism of Israel’s violence against Palestinians has drawn outsized attention in both the primary and the general election campaigns.

When asked by a reporter at the caucus meeting Saturday about his message to Jewish voters who are concerned about his past comments, El-Sayed said that “he believes in the safety and the dignity of Jewish kids like I believe in the safety and dignity of my own kids.”

“We have to come together as folks who understand what it's like to be told we're not enough-of,” El-Sayed said. “We have to come together around our mutual safety, and that is something I am committed to. So I'm looking forward to continuing that conversation. As I've always said, if you invite me in, I will come. We may not always agree, but I want to be able to demonstrate how we can disagree agreeably.”
entries.author: Manuela Silva

entries.title: After a Much-Needed Win, the Spirit Hopes to Regain Momentum
entries.summary: Sunday’s 1-0 victory over Bay FC was the team’s first win in more than a month.
entries.content:
With little room to spare, the Washington Spirit earned its first win of August on Sunday.

Washington defeated Bay FC 1-0 for the team’s first victory since July 29, behind Paige Metayer’s 45th-minute goal. The win kept the Spirit in second place in the NWSL standings at 40 points, with Utah and San Diego both tied for third with 39 points. Gotham FC leads the league with 45 points.

The victory also keeps the Spirit undefeated against Bay FC in their seven meetings.

Washington had struggled since defeating Utah 1-0 on July 29. The Spirit lost 1-0 to San Diego on Aug. 2, 4-3 to North Carolina on Aug. 8 and 1-0 to Orlando on Aug. 23, with an Aug. 16 tie with Angel City FC accounting for the team’s lone point in the standings prior to Sunday.

The Spirit’s slide coincided with a surge from Gotham, which has posted four wins and two ties since July 29. That stretch allowed Gotham to overtake Washington atop the league standings.

Sunday provided Washington a good opportunity to get back on track: Entering the match, Bay FC had just one win in its previous six contests. But the California-based squad earned Sunday’s first real chance, as Karlie Lema’s shot hit off the crossbar in the 40th minute.

Shortly after, the Spirit got on the board. In the 45th minute, Trinity Rodman took a quick feed on the left side of the field and maneuvered her way through a pair of defenders and into the box. Rodman’s left-footed shot hit off the crossbar and landed on the goal line, but officials let play continue and Metayer scored off the rebound. It was the midfielder’s first goal of the season.

With two months remaining in the regular season and the winless streak now in the rearview, Washington will face a schedule that should allow them to stay within striking distance of Gotham. After a match against the Portland Thorns, who are currently fifth in the NWSL standings, the team’s next four meetings are against Boston, Chicago, Angel City FC and Houston, all of which are currently outside the league’s playoff race.
entries.author: Alex Schiffer

entries.title: Pentagon Pushes Back on Report of Military Concerns About Iran
entries.summary: The Washington Post says top military leaders warned the defense secretary against extending the Iran war. That’s inaccurate, the Pentagon counters.
entries.content:
The Pentagon is pushing back against a report that military leaders are warning that a sustained, large-scale military operation against Iran is unsustainable and risks America’s ability to confront threats across the globe and at home.

The Washington Post reported Sunday that several military leaders — including the Navy’s top admiral and the commanders overseeing Europe, Asia and Latin America — warned Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth they don’t agree with keeping forces deployed to the Middle East through September and possibly into 2027. The chiefs of the Army and Air Force agreed with extending their forces but said doing so comes with significant risk.

The commanders raised concerns about ships, aircraft and munitions being redirected to support the Iran operation, saying that is limiting missions and training elsewhere. The operation, which just passed the six-month mark, is straining maintenance and readiness, while the war has drained key munitions, according to outside experts

Their warnings were included in the Aug. 14 Secretary of Defense Orders Book,

a classified document used to allocate forces around the world and collect military leaders’ assessments of the risks associated with those decisions, the Post reported. It said the objections were recorded as “non-concurs,” meaning the leaders disagreed but would still carry out the orders.

The Post cited unnamed people familiar with the document who spoke on the condition of anonymity because it is classified.

“Publishing highly classified assessments from the Secretary’s orders book is a crime,” Pentagon spokesperson Sean Parnell said Sunday.

“It’s a betrayal of the force,” Parnell, an assistant secretary of defense, said in a post on X. “And much of what they’re publishing is inaccurate. Of course, we demand candid military advice. Non-concurs are standard. The Secretary sees them constantly. That’s how you run a real military.”

Parnell said the Post’s reporting “isn’t about readiness” but about “they hate President Trump and Secretary Hegseth more than they love America.”

The Washington Post defended its reporting as accurate and legal.“We’re confident in our reporting, our sourcing and the protections that guarantee the rights of news organizations to publish information in the public interest that holds officials accountable,” Olivia Petersen, a spokesperson for the newspaper, said in a statement on X. “The assertion that such publication is a crime is both incorrect and irresponsible.”

On Capitol Hill, Rep. Gil Cisneros (D-California), a former undersecretary of defense for personnel and readiness, said the Post’s report is troubling.

“If this article is true, it is just another example of mismanagement by Pete Hegseth. He continues to make decisions against the advice of senior leaders without regard for the effect it will have on personnel and equipment,” Cisneros said in a post on X. “He either does not comprehend the consequences of his decisions, or he just doesn’t give a damn. Unfortunately, his decisions today will have a negative impact on readiness for years to come.”

Separately, Rep. Raja Krishnamoorthi (D-Illinois), a senior member of the House Intelligence Committee, said the war with Iran is straining military readiness. Asked on Bloomberg on Sunday whether the U.S. is prepared for a conflict with China, he said, “No, we’re not.”

He pointed to the movement of the carrier USS George Washington from the Pacific to the Middle East, and what he described as the “depletion” of Patriot missiles and other munitions needed to deter Russia and China. Noting that China’s president wants his military to be ready to invade Taiwan by 2027, he said the U.S. is “in a dangerous window.”

“We're going to invite aggression by the Chinese, and I think they are counting our magazine depth every day, the number of munitions we have, where our troops are stationed,” Krishnamoorthi said. “And they notice, and that only causes them to consider more seriously potentially moving on Taiwan.”
